This prospective study compares outcomes of non-surgical treatment regimens, including interventional anaesthetic techniques or radiofrequency thermocoagulation, with a coccygectomy after one year. Patients with coccygodynia scheduled for an outpatient evaluation in a single institution completed a baseline questionnaire scoring pain (Numerical Rating Scale, NRS, range 0-10), functional impairment (Oswestry Disability Index, ODI, range 0-100) and health-related quality of life (Short-Form 12-Item Survey-version 2, SF-12v2, range 0-100). They were then offered continuation of a multimodal conservative management or a coccygectomy. One-year NRS, ODI, and SF-12v2 scores were compared between groups using analysis of covariance, adjusted for baseline scores and age. A total of 139 patients with coccygodynia were evaluated between May 2020 and December 2023, of whom 72 patients fulfilled inclusion criteria. One year follow-up data of 59 patients were analysed (surgical n = 35, conservative n = 24, 83% response rate). After adjustment for baseline values and age, patients who underwent coccygectomy reported significantly lower pain scores (NRS: B = - 2.39, P = 0.004) and disability scores (ODI: B = - 13.22, P = 0.005) and significantly higher mental health scores (SF-12 MCS: B = 3.06, P = 0.011) at one year compared with patients who continued conservative treatment. No significant between-group difference was observed for SF-12v2 physical health scores (B = 1.46, P = 0.636). At one-year follow-up, patients who underwent coccygectomy demonstrated greater improvement in pain, functional impairment, and mental health outcomes than patients who continued conservative
